claims: Section 1 of the 25th Amendment explicitly states that if the President is removed, dies, or resigns, the Vice President becomes President.
Section 2 of the 25th Amendment allows the President to nominate a Vice President, confirmed by a majority of both Houses of Congress, if a vacancy occurs.

Section 3 of the 25th Amendment allows the President to declare in writing they are temporarily unable to discharge their duties, making the Vice President Acting President until a written declaration to the contrary is submitted.
Section 4 of the 25th Amendment allows the Vice President and a majority of the Cabinet to declare the President incapacitated, immediately elevating the Vice President to Acting President.

If the President disputes the declaration under Section 4 of the 25th Amendment, Congress decides the issue, requiring a two-thirds vote in both houses to maintain the Vice President as Acting President.
The 25th Amendment was created following the assassination of John F. Kennedy.
The 25th Amendment was created to address gaps in the Constitution regarding presidential disability.
The 25th Amendment was created to provide a clear procedure to remove a President unfit for office.
The removal clause (Section 4) of the 25th Amendment has never been invoked.
In 1973, Vice President Gerald Ford was confirmed under Section 2 following Spiro Agnew's resignation.
In 1974, Gerald Ford assumed the presidency under Section 1 following Richard Nixon's resignation.
In 1985, President Ronald Reagan briefly transferred power to Vice President George H.W. Bush during surgery.
In 2002 and 2007, President George W. Bush transferred power to Vice President Dick Cheney during medical procedures.
